h: Building a Seafront Day Around the Sharks
p: SEA LIFE Blackpool sits on the Central Promenade, in the same building as Madame Tussauds Blackpool and a short stroll from the Tower. Several of Blackpool's big-name attractions, including the Tower, SEA LIFE, Madame Tussauds and the Blackpool Dungeon, are run by the same operator, so it's worth looking at combined tickets if you're planning to do more than one. They can make a real difference to the cost of a family weekend.

For the visit itself, allow somewhere between an hour and a half and two hours, depending on how long your crew lingers at the tanks. Toddlers often get the most out of it, as everything is at a slow, peaceful pace with plenty to point at. Older children tend to enjoy the keeper talks, where they can ask questions about what the sharks eat and how the team looks after them.

Buggies are generally fine on the route, though it's sensible to check access details before you go if you're bringing a wheelchair or a double pushchair. The tunnel is often the busiest spot, so if you want a calmer look, let the crowd move ahead and hang back a moment.

Once you're out, the seafront is right on your doorstep. Fancy more creatures? Blackpool Zoo, out on the east side of town, is a bigger day out with everything from big cats to sea lions. And if the weather turns, the Tower Ballroom tea dances and the arcades along the Golden Mile are only a short walk away, though the bigger amusements and adult gaming centres are strictly for over-18s.
